title: Cottage cheese, full fat, large or small curd

content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese is a soft, mildly acidic dairy product obtained by curdling milk and separating the whey. Full‑fat cottage cheese contains about 20 % fat, and the curd size can be large or small depending on the manufacturing process.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods; it was made in ancient Egypt.
Large curd is produced by longer settling and coarser stirring, while small curd results from finer chopping.
In Russia cottage cheese is traditionally served with sour cream, honey, berries, or used in baked dishes.
It is widely used as a base for cheese pancakes, dumpling fillings, and various diet recipes.
In some countries, such as Poland, cottage cheese is called "twarożek" and features in traditional cuisine.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides about 12–14 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in cottage cheese helps maintain strong bones and teeth and supports nerve function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Full‑fat cottage cheese has virtually no sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and moderate fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cottage cheese contains lactose; people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Full‑fat cottage cheese contains about 20 % fat, so portion control is advised for calorie‑conscious diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties are salted; those with hypertension should opt for unsalted versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be eaten plain, mixed into smoothies, used for cheese pancakes, casseroles, stuffed in crepes or dumplings, or blended into sauces and dips. For a sweeter taste, combine it with honey, fruit, or berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container. It is usually good for 5‑7 days after opening. Discard if it develops an off‑odor, discoloration, or mold.
